main_text.p: quæ odio mali & studio boni constat,re-cenfetur: ut ex hoc uerfu liquet. Nos de his ordine agemus.
main_text.head: DE SACCO, SEU DE lugubri habitu,
main_text.p: 1. Visitatissimum fuit iam olim apud Is-raelitas, sacco, seu uili & lugubri habitu uti,si quando uel publicæ uel priuatæ ca-lamitates ansam præberent. In exequijs Abneri dolo perempti: Scindite, dicebat Rex Dauid ad suos familiares, ueftimen-ta ueftra, & accingite uos saccis, & plan-gite ante Abner; 2.Sam,3.31. Et in hifto-ria Nehemiæ, cap.9.1. Vicefimaquarta die menfis huius,congregauerunt fefe fi-lij Israelis in jeiunio,& cum saccis,ac ter-ra erat super eos,&c. Hunc morem ri-tumq; etiam Ethnici quidam nonnun-quam observasse uidentur,ut Plutarchus περὶ δεισιδαιμονίας, his uerbis hominem su-perstitiosum graphicè depingens, docet: ἐξω νηστείαν φανιον ἐχων, ἢ περιεσπασμένος ῥάκεσι ῥυπαροῖς, πολλάκις δὲ γυναικὸς ἐν πηλῷ κυλινδούμενος. Fortassis inde ortum duxit proverbium, Vestem mutare: quod luctus indi-cium est.
2. De causa finali sacci citra superstitio

page.notes: Greek quotation is partly illegible in the scan; the Greek words, especially after "ἐξω", are reconstructed with uncertainty and should be checked against Plutarch's De superstitione. The Greek title before "his uerbis" is also uncertain. The printed heading reads "SEV", corrected to "SEU" per the u/v rule. The printed "Is-" and "Israelis" are kept as printed, as are the hyphens "re-", "ca-", "ter-", "ri-", "nonnun-", "prouer-", "indi-", "su-", "ueftimen-", "plan-", "hifto-", "fi-", and "superstitio-" (line-end hyphen after "superstitio" is not printed; the last word stays as printed, with the catchword "nem" below). Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Printed paragraph number "1." and "2." are kept as paragraph openers.
